chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi from Ali ibn Asbat, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, begins by looking at the visitors of the grave of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) on the afternoon of Arafah.
He (the narrator) said: I asked, 'Before He looks at the people of the standing (at Arafah)?' He said, 'Yes.'
I asked, 'And how is that?' He said, 'Because among those (people of Arafah) are children of fornication, and among these (visitors of Karbala) there are no children of fornication.'

key_terms.زُوَّارِ قَبْرِ الْحُسَیْنِ: visitors of the grave of al-Husayn

ai.seo_question: Why does Allah look at visitors of Imam Husain's grave before the pilgrims of Arafah?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this unique distinction where divine attention precedes the general audience at Arafah, emphasizing the spiritual purity of Ziyarat al-Husayn. The scholarly interpretation of 'children of fornication' (awlad al-zina) in this context often refers to the broader human condition or specific historical figures, contrasting with the devoted visitors who are spiritually cleansed through their connection to the Imam. This highlights the intercessory power of Imam Husayn’s shrine as a locus of divine mercy that supersedes even the central ritual of Hajj.
